top.text: A clinical assessment is recommended. A nurse can visit you at home to look at your balance, medicines, eyesight, home and more.
Strength and balance exercise is the best-proven way to reduce falls. Join a structured programme such as a supervised class, Tai Chi or a physiotherapist-led plan.
Book a nurse home visit to look at your risk in more detail.

all.text: A clinical assessment is recommended. A nurse can visit you at home to look at your balance, medicines, eyesight, home and more.
Strength and balance exercise is the best-proven way to reduce falls. Join a structured programme such as a supervised class, Tai Chi or a physiotherapist-led plan.
Book a nurse home visit to look at your risk in more detail.
Some medicines can make falls more likely. Do not stop any medicine on your own. Ask a pharmacist or doctor to review all your medicines, including herbal ones.
Feeling dizzy when you stand up should be checked. Stand up slowly and tell a nurse or doctor.
Make your home safer. Fix or remove the hazards you ticked, add handrails and non-slip mats, and keep a rechargeable lamp or torch for power cuts.
Have your eyes checked every year. If you wear multifocal glasses, take extra care outside and on stairs.
Wear well-fitting shoes with a firm sole and grip. See a nurse or foot specialist about foot pain or numbness.
Bladder urgency and night-time toilet trips can lead to falls. A nurse or doctor can help.
Pain or stiffness that makes walking harder can often be treated. Speak to a nurse, physiotherapist or doctor.
A hearing check is worthwhile. Hearing problems are linked to falls.
Ask a physiotherapist or nurse to check that your walking aid fits you and to show you how to use it.
Memory or thinking changes are worth discussing with a doctor. Ask a family member or carer to help with this assessment.
Take care on uneven paths, drains and steps. Choose well-lit routes and use support where you can.
Build up gradually to 150 minutes of activity a week, including balance and strength exercises.
Regular, balanced meals help keep muscles and bones strong. Tell a nurse or doctor if you are losing weight without trying.
